newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE AND WHALERS TIE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE AND WHALERS TIE.

text.p: Eric Lacroix, Adam Deadmarsh and Sandis Ozolinsh scored in the third period as the Colorado Avalanche rallied for a 4-4 tie with the Hartford Whalers in a battle of first-place teams Saturday.
Lacroix sparked the comeback with his second goal of the game, a power-play tally with 9:23 remaining. Deadmarsh sliced the margin to 4-3 with 5:30 to go.
"We were fortunate to turn it around tonight," Deadmarsh said. "I think it comes down to work ethic. If you want to win, you have to be the one to work the hardest."
In Montreal, Shane Corson had a pair of goals and Jocelyn Thibault stopped 38 shots as the Montreal Canadiens routed the Vancouver Canucks, 6-1.
Vincent Damphousse added a goal and an assist and Saku Koivu and Stephane Richer had two assists apiece for the Canadiens.
At New Jersey, Brian Rolston had a hat trick and John MacLean scored twice in the five-goal third period that rallied the New Jersey Devils to a 6-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Rolston's first career hat trick helped New Jersey to its sixth win in seven games and sent Tampa Bay to its fifth straight game without a victory.
At the Islanders, Bruce Gardiner scored his first two NHL goals in the third period and Damian Rhodes made 24 saves, leading the Ottawa Senators to a 4-1 victory over the New York Islanders.
Tom Chorske also scored in the third period for the Senators, who have posted consecutive wins for the first time this season.
In Philadelphia, Greg Hawgood's power-play goal with 2:37 remaining capped a third-period rally and lifted the San Jose Sharks into a 2-2 tie with the Philadelphia Flyers.

Philadelphia's Daniel Lacroix had 54 seconds left on his high-sticking penalty when Hawgood fired a wrist shot from the right faceoff circle that hit goaltender Garth Snow's left pad and trickled past his glove side.
Red-hot John LeClair scored twice in the first period for Philadelphia and has nine goals in his last seven games.
In Pittsburgh, Mark Messier had two goals and an assist and the New York Rangers used a six-goal second period to snap a five-game winless streak and bury the floundering Pittsburgh Penguins, 8-3.
Adam Graves added a goal and two assists for the Rangers, who have outscored Pittsburgh, 16-4, in two wins this year.
In St Louis, Grant Fuhr stopped 21 shots for his first shutout of the season and 18th of his career and Geoff Courtnall set up both goals as the St. Louis Blues blanked the Calgary Flames, 2-0.
Harry York's sixth goal of the season, 3:41 into the second period, gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead it would not relinquish.

In Phoenix, Jeremy Roenick had his first multi-goal game of the season and capped a third-period comeback as the Phoenix Coyotes won at home for the first time in nearly five weeks, defeating the Toronto Maple Leafs, 3-2.
Roenick, acquired from Chicago in a pre-season deal, had struggled through a prolonged holdout and had managed just one goal in his first 12 games.

In Buffalo, the game between the Boston Bruins and Buffalo Sabres at Buffalo's Marine Midland Arena was postponed due to the collapse of the Jumbotron scoreboard onto the ice surface. There were no injuries.
